_note: Things to do around each destination (day spots — NOT standalone destinations). Key = destination id from places.json. Fields: n name, k kind (forest|water|temple|heritage|village|view|hike|wildlife|experience), m approx drive minutes from the destination (0 = walkable), h time needed, d what it is (1-2 lines), t practical tip (optional), b best months (optional), busy 1 = popular/crowded spot (optional), q map search text if the name alone is ambiguous (optional). Batch 1 (Nov 2026): Shimla + Solan districts, checked against current sources. Edit freely — the site reads this file directly. img = Wikimedia Commons file name (shown via Special:FilePath, credited to by + Commons link); spots without img show the coloured card.

87.d: Grey-stone mansion from 1888 on Observatory Hill, where key talks before Partition took place. A short guided tour covers the grand halls; the lawns alone are worth the visit.
87.t: Closed on Mondays and national holidays.

87.d: Pahari miniature paintings, old temple woodwork, coins and textiles in a colonial house near Chaura Maidan. A calm hour away from the Mall.
Hilltop temple of Goddess Tara south of Shimla, reached by road or a steep forest path. Wide views over the Shimla hills, and far fewer people than Jakhu.
A forest trail from the Summer Hill side down to a tall waterfall. At its best during and just after the monsoon — in dry months it can be a trickle.
A deep, shaded deodar forest below Annandale with a stream running through it — one of the few quiet corners left inside Shimla.
Untouched deodar and oak forest that has fed Shimla's water by gravity for over a century. Protected since 1952, a sanctuary since 1990, and almost empty on weekdays.
87.t: Walks start near Charabara. Check the entry rules at the forest gate before going in.
87.img: Entrance ,Shimla Water Catchment Wildlife Sanctuary, Himachal Pardes, India.JPG

127.d: Untouched deodar and oak forest that has fed Shimla's water by gravity for over a century — the only undisturbed middle-altitude forest left in these lower hills. Listen for koklass pheasants.
127.t: Walks start near Charabara. Check the entry rules at the forest gate before going in.
127.img: Entrance ,Shimla Water Catchment Wildlife Sanctuary, Himachal Pardes, India.JPG

127.d: The President's summer retreat at Chharabra — an old wooden building with lawns and orchards, open to visitors since 2023.
127.t: Book online or at the counter. Closed on Mondays and public holidays; last entry 3 pm.

127.d: A small village below Mashobra with an old temple in a deodar grove. Known for the village fair held there every May.
The lone 2,870 m peak behind Mashobra, with the Shali Mata temple on top. About 7 km one way from Khatnol village through blue pine and deodar, then a 360° view of the Himalaya.
127.t: Start early and carry food and water — there's nothing on the trail.

89.d: A quiet ridge village past Kufri on the Theog road — potato fields, apple orchards and clear morning views. What Kufri felt like before the crowds.
The protected forest right below Kufri that supplies Shimla's water. Deodar, oak and silence — a complete contrast to Kufri's pony tracks.
89.t: Walks start near Charabara. Check the entry rules at the forest gate.
89.img: Entrance ,Shimla Water Catchment Wildlife Sanctuary, Himachal Pardes, India.JPG

89.d: The high point above Kufri, with snow-range views on a clear day. Reached on foot or by pony.
89.t: Walk if you can — the pony track gets muddy and crowded.
89.img: Himalayan mountains, Kufri, Himachal Pradesh, India (2017).jpg

89.d: A high-altitude zoo with Himalayan animals and pheasants, including the state bird, the western tragopan.
89.img: Bear of Himalayan Nature Park, Kufri.jpg

69.d: A lone 2,870 m peak with the Shali Mata temple on top. About 7 km one way from Khatnol village through blue pine and deodar, with a 360° view at the end.
69.t: Start early and carry food and water.

69.d: Untouched deodar and oak forest that feeds Shimla's water — one of the quietest walks in the region.
69.t: Walks start near Charabara. Check the entry rules at the forest gate.
69.img: Entrance ,Shimla Water Catchment Wildlife Sanctuary, Himachal Pardes, India.JPG

69.d: The President's summer retreat at Chharabra — an old wooden building with lawns and orchards, open to visitors.
69.t: Closed on Mondays and public holidays; last entry 3 pm.

26.d: A small, still lake ringed by deodars with a Nag Devta temple at one end. The forest department runs a small eco park here, and the village holds a fair by the lake every year.
26.t: Small entry fee for the eco park. No boating.
26.img: Reflection in Tani Jubbar Lake at Narkanda.jpg

26.d: A wide open meadow on the flank of Hatu, a 20-minute forest walk from the Hatu temple. Locals link it to the Pandavas; most people who reach Hatu never walk this far.
26.t: The Hatu road is narrow and steep — small cars only. Snowbound Dec–Feb.
26.img: View of peaks from the way to Hatu Peak, Narkanda.jpg

26.d: Where Satyanand Stokes brought new apple varieties and started the orchards that changed Himachal's economy. The family still runs the farm.

66.d: The orchard where Satyanand Stokes started Himachal's apple story, and the Paramjyoti temple he built nearby. Ask at the farm about apple products and seasonal visits.
A small deodar-ringed lake with a Nag Devta temple at one end and a forest department eco park around it.
66.t: Small entry fee for the eco park. No boating.
66.img: Reflection in Tani Jubbar Lake at Narkanda.jpg

66.d: A wide meadow a 20-minute forest walk beyond the Hatu temple, with big views and almost nobody around.
66.t: Small cars only on the Hatu road. Snowbound Dec–Feb.
66.img: View of peaks from the way to Hatu Peak, Narkanda.jpg

27.d: A wide open meadow on the right flank of the peak, about 20 minutes' walk from the temple through deodar and oak. The best picnic spot on Hatu.
27.img: View of peaks from the way to Hatu Peak, Narkanda.jpg

27.d: Rock formations a short walk from the Hatu temple, which locals say the Pandavas used as a stove during their exile.
A small deodar-ringed lake with a Nag Devta temple, on the road down towards Thanedar.
27.t: Small entry fee for the eco park.
27.img: Reflection in Tani Jubbar Lake at Narkanda.jpg

65.d: An old stone temple of Hateshwari Mata on the banks of the Pabbar, one of the most important shrines in upper Shimla.
65.img: Varun Shiv Kapur, Hateshwari Temple in Hatkoti.jpg

65.d: From Kharapathar, a 7 km dirt track climbs through deodar and spruce to an old temple at the source of the Giri river. Fit walkers can carry on 2–3 hours up to the Kuppar meadow.
65.t: Very few people even in season. Carry food — only basic dhabas near the temple.

65.d: Slow walks along the Pabbar through apple country. The river is known for trout.
65.t: Angling needs a permit from the fisheries department — ask locally.

70.d: An old stone temple of Hateshwari Mata beside the Pabbar river, the most revered shrine in this valley.
70.img: Varun Shiv Kapur, Hateshwari Temple in Hatkoti.jpg

70.d: A 7 km forest track from Kharapathar to the old temple at the source of the Giri river — temple built by the Jubbal rulers. Kuppar meadow is 2–3 hours further up.
70.t: Carry food. The track is dirt and can be slushy after rain.

70.d: A small ridge town at about 2,700 m on the Shimla–Rohru road, surrounded by apple orchards. Good for an evening view and a cup of tea.

67.d: The last village on the Rohru side before the climb to Chanshal — a good place to stop, check road conditions and eat.
Twin villages beyond the pass in one of the most remote corners of Shimla district, cut off by snow for months every year.
67.t: Only when the pass is open. Ask in Rohru or Larot about the road the day before.

68.d: A breeding centre for the western tragopan, Himachal's rare state bird, which bred in captivity for the first time in the world here.
68.t: Closed on Mondays and during breeding season (April–August).
68.img: Captive Tragopan melanocephalus (male) at Sarahan Pheasantry Himachal Pradesh JEG8442.jpg

68.d: The palace of the former Bushahr rulers in Rampur, with carved wood and stone on the banks of the Sutlej.
68.t: Still owned by the royal family — you may only see it from outside.

71.d: Hilltop temple of Goddess Tara just above Shoghi, with wide views over the Shimla hills.
The 1888 stone mansion on Shimla's Observatory Hill where key talks before Partition were held. Guided tour plus big lawns.
71.t: Closed on Mondays and national holidays.

88.d: A white temple of Goddess Kali on a hilltop about 7 km from Chail. On a clear day you see the snow range on one side and Churdhar on the other.
A riverside stop on the Ashwini on the way up from Kandaghat, where dhabas put tables right in the shallow stream.
88.t: Don't wade in after heavy rain — the water rises fast.
88.img: Ashwani Khadd or rivulet at Sadhu Pul ,near Chail ,Himachal Pradesh.jpg

88.d: The Maharaja of Patiala's old summer palace, now a heritage hotel, set in deodar forest. Walk the grounds or have tea on the lawns.
88.img: The Palace at Chail near Shimla.jpg

90.d: A quiet cliff-edge path through pine and oak, popular with birdwatchers early in the morning.
90.t: Parts of Kasauli are Air Force area — stay on the trail.

90.d: A small 19th-century church on the Mall with old stained glass — a calm stop on a heritage walk.
The highest hill around Solan, about 5–6 km up from Chambaghat through grassland and forest to a narrow cave and a Kali temple on top.
90.t: Carry a head torch for the cave, and start early.

91.d: A cantonment jail from 1849, with its cells and stories kept as a small museum.
A quiet colonial-era graveyard on the edge of town with old gravestones and big views.
The highest hill around Solan — 5–6 km up from Chambaghat to a narrow cave and a Kali temple on top, with views to Churdhar.
91.t: Carry a head torch for the cave.

92.d: Temple of Solan's patron goddess. Her three-day fair every June is the town's biggest event.
The highest hill around Solan — 5–6 km up from Chambaghat to a narrow cave and a Kali temple on top.
92.t: Carry a head torch for the cave.

93.d: The highest hill around Solan, about 5–6 km up from Chambaghat through grassland and forest to a narrow cave and a Kali temple on top.
93.t: Carry a head torch for the cave, and start early.

93.d: Temple of Solan's patron goddess. Her three-day fair every June is the town's biggest event.

94.d: A deodar-forested valley at about 2,000 m, with apple and peach orchards and almost no tourism. A trail goes on to Churdhar for the fit.
94.t: There's a forest rest house; book through the HP eco-tourism site.

94.d: A shrine of Shirgul Devta, the most revered deity of this region, about 10 km from Habban.
Rajgarh is known as the peach valley — in spring the slopes around town turn pink. Ask your host which orchards welcome walkers.

113.d: The temple of Kullu's chief deity, brought from Ayodhya in the 1600s. During Dussehra every god of the valley comes to pay respects to Raghunath.
A carved stone Shiva temple from around the 9th century, one of the oldest in the Kullu valley, standing quietly in the fields near Bajaura.
113.img: 0042523 Basheshar Mahadev Temple, Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh 005.jpg

113.d: A week-long gathering of hundreds of village deities carried in palanquins to the Dhalpur ground — the biggest festival in Himachal.
113.t: Dates follow the Hindu calendar; stays fill up months ahead.

113.d: Watch handlooms weave the famous patterned Kullu shawls and caps at the weavers' cooperatives around Bhuntar and Kullu.
113.t: Buy from cooperatives, not roadside 'factory outlets'.

143.d: A carved stone Shiva temple from around the 9th century, one of the oldest in the Kullu valley.
143.img: 0042523 Basheshar Mahadev Temple, Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh 005.jpg

143.d: Bhuntar sits where the Parvati joins the Beas — walk down to the riverside to see the two colours of water meet.
Weavers' cooperatives around Bhuntar make the famous patterned Kullu shawls and caps on handlooms.
143.t: Buy from cooperatives, not roadside 'factory outlets'.

86.d: A tall waterfall above Vashisht village, reached by a 2–3 km walk through orchards and pine. The best short walk from Manali.
86.t: The path is slippery near the falls — good shoes.

86.d: A small cave near Prini village on the left bank of the Beas, linked to Arjuna's meditation in the Mahabharata. A 20-minute uphill walk from the road.
A colourful Tibetan monastery near the Manali bus stand, built by refugees in the late 1960s. Calm, and right in town.
A four-tiered wooden pagoda temple from 1553 inside a deodar forest — Manali's most famous sight.
86.t: Go before 9 am to beat the queues.

134.d: The temple of Manu at the top of Old Manali village — climb through the old wooden houses to reach it.
Giant deodars between Old Manali and the Hidimba temple — walk through the forest instead of taking the road.
A four-tiered wooden pagoda temple from 1553 in the Dhungri forest.
134.t: Go before 9 am to beat the queues.

111.d: A tall waterfall above the village, reached by a 2–3 km walk through orchards and pine forest.
111.t: Slippery near the falls — good shoes.

117.d: A walk up from Solang to a cave-temple under a waterfall; in winter the water freezes into a natural ice lingam.

138.d: A waterfall fed by glacier melt just above Kothi on the old Rohtang road — cold, loud and impressive in early summer.
The Beas squeezes through a deep, narrow gorge right below the village — look down from the bridge.

137.d: Old shikhara-style Shiva and Gayatri Devi temples from the time when Jagatsukh was the capital of Kullu.

112.d: A 500-year-old castle of stone and wood, built in the earthquake-proof kath-kuni style, with valley views from its balcony.
The home of painter Nicholas Roerich, with his Himalayan paintings and the Urusvati folk art museum next door.
A pagoda-style wooden temple with layered roofs in the upper village.
A waterfall beside Jana village up the hill from Naggar, with dhabas serving siddu and local food.

122.d: One of the oldest trout farms in Himachal, on the Beas — see the ponds and buy fresh trout.
A 500-year-old castle of stone and wood across the river, with valley views.

63.d: An old stone temple near the gurudwara, one of several shrines around the hot springs.

28.d: Walk up the valley past the last fields towards the glacier and the snow peaks at the head of the Tosh nala.

23.d: An old deodar forest just above Pulga with mossy trunks and filtered light — the reason many people stay in Pulga.

11.d: An old, mossy deodar forest a short walk from Kalga — quiet, especially in the morning.

36.d: A waterfall in the forest a short walk from the road between Gushaini and Banjar.
A small government trout farm on the Tirthan, where the valley's trout are raised.
36.t: Angling in the Tirthan needs a fisheries permit — ask your host.

16.d: A forest waterfall a short walk from the Banjar road.
A small trout farm on the Tirthan river.

31.d: A small waterfall in the forest close to Jibhi village, with a wooden walkway and a pool.
The temple of Shringa Rishi, the most revered deity of the Banjar area, in a pine forest above the valley.

32.d: A 3 km walk from Jalori Pass to the ruins of an old fort on a grassy ridge, with Himalayan views on every side.

33.d: A 3 km walk west from the pass to old fort ruins on an open meadow ridge.

15.d: A cascade in the forest about 3 km from Shangarh village, through orchards and small villages.
The deity who protects the Shangarh meadow — locals say he sheltered the Pandavas. Rules here are strict: no shoes or loud noise on the meadow.

121.d: One of the most important old temples of the Sutlej valley, linked to Parshuram, with fine wood carving.
An old temple of the goddess Ambika in the heritage lanes of Nirmand.

25.d: The home and studio of painter Sobha Singh, known for his portraits of Sikh Gurus and Sohni-Mahiwal.
A studio where you can watch potters at work, and sometimes join a short session.

58.d: A small deodar-ringed lake between Naddi and McLeod Ganj, with a Shiva temple on its bank.

59.d: A small temple above Dharamkot where the Triund trail begins — walk this far for the views even if you're not doing Triund.

62.d: A Shiva temple with a natural stone lingam in two parts, at the meeting of the Beas and Choch rivers near Indora.

77.d: A large Tibetan monastery with a tall stupa in Bir's Tibetan colony.
A big monastery in the pine forest near Bir, seat of a major Tibetan lama.
Walk through the tea gardens around Bir — at their best in the soft evening light.

78.d: Walk through the tea gardens and visit the cooperative tea factory to see how Kangra tea is made.
A riverside gorge just outside Palampur, with Dhauladhar views and a café on the cliff.
A peaceful Tibetan monastery village between Palampur and Baijnath.

79.d: A peaceful Tibetan monastery village between Baijnath and Palampur.

80.d: One of the most important Devi temples of Kangra, in the old town.

82.d: A stone church from 1852 in the deodars between McLeod Ganj and Forsyth Ganj, with Belgian stained glass.
82.q: St John in the Wilderness Church
82.img: St. John in the Wilderness churchyard, McLeod Ganj, India - September 2014.jpg

82.d: The story of Tibet and its people in exile, inside the main temple complex.
A small lake with a Shiva temple on the way to Naddi.

83.d: Gardens and workshops where Tibetan arts — thangka painting, wood carving, embroidery — are kept alive.
Kangra miniature paintings, old coins and tribal costumes near the main bus stand.
A memorial park in the pine forest for soldiers of Himachal.

145.d: Kangra miniature paintings, old coins and tribal costumes near the main bus stand.
Gardens and workshops where Tibetan arts are kept alive.
A Shiva temple by a stream in the forest near Khaniyara, quiet and cool.

84.d: India's first notified heritage village and its neighbour — old mansions, cobbled lanes and a village tank.

115.d: Climb past the Bhagsu waterfall to the small cafés above it, with views back over the valley.

105.d: The big new monastery in Kaza town, with bright murals.

107.d: Meditation caves cut into the cliff above the village, used by monks for centuries.

38.d: A steep walk of about an hour up from the monastery to a small high lake with views of the Spiti and Pin valleys.
38.t: You are above 4,000 m — go slowly.

51.d: The main monastery of the Pin valley, of the Nyingma tradition.
The last village in the Pin valley, where the road ends and the Pin-Parvati and Bhaba trails begin.

43.d: A long waterfall dropping off the cliffs above Sissu, best when the snow melts.

109.d: One of the biggest and most important monasteries in Lahaul, on the slope across the river from Keylong.
A monastery on a ridge above Keylong, known for its masked dance in summer.

108.d: A plain-looking temple hiding some of the finest old wood carving in Himachal.

54.d: A traditional village a short drive from Kalpa, reached on a road cut into a sheer cliff with Kinner Kailash across the valley.
A Kinnauri wooden temple in the old part of Kalpa.

41.d: A tower-like wooden fort-temple above Sangla, once the seat of the Bushahr rulers.
41.t: Cover your head and wear the cap given at the gate.
41.img: Kamru Fort, Kamru village, Sangla Valley, Himachal Pradesh 02.jpg

41.d: A pretty Kinnauri village of wooden houses and a carved temple, below Sangla.

45.d: The village goddess's carved wooden temple in the middle of Chitkul.
Walk out beyond the village along the Baspa towards the border — the road ends, the mountains close in.

37.d: A centuries-old naturally preserved monk's mummy in Gue village, just inside Spiti.
37.t: Foreign travellers need an Inner Line Permit on this stretch; everyone should carry ID.

10.d: Ribba is known for its grapes and homemade angoori wine — ask your host about the vineyards.

74.d: A group of carved stone temples from the 10th century onwards, in the heart of Chamba.
74.img: Lakshmi Narayan Temples in a row (6132466715).jpg

74.d: Chamba rumals, Pahari paintings and old copper plates from the Chamba kingdom.
A wooden temple on a ridge above the town with the best view over Chamba and the Ravi.
Fine double-sided embroidery that looks the same on both sides — watch it being made and buy from the artisans.

72.d: Small falls and streams in the forest just below Dalhousie, with a memorial to Sardar Ajit Singh.
Seven springs meeting in the forest, said to carry mica that helps the skin.
Dalhousie's oldest church, from 1863, near Gandhi Chowk.
A quiet circular road through deodar forest on the highest part of town.

73.d: A 12th-century wooden temple at the edge of the meadow, with carvings of the Pandavas.
73.img: Khajjiar naag mandir, Khajjiar at Chamba Himachal Pradesh.jpg

55.d: A walk of about 3 km up from Bharmour to a temple on a high meadow — pilgrims stop here before Manimahesh.
Bharmour is the home of the Gaddi shepherds — ask your host to meet a family and see their wool and flocks.

1.d: One of the remotest villages of Pangi, at the end of a road from Killar.
1.t: Roads can close with landslides; ask in Killar.

1.d: The most revered goddess temple of Pangi.

4.d: A six-storey fort of wood and stone on a high stone base — the old capital of Suket, with the Mahamaya temple on top.
An old goddess temple about 7 km from Karsog with fine wood carving.

139.d: An old goddess temple near Karsog with fine wood carving.
A six-storey fort of wood and stone, the old capital of Suket, with the Mahamaya temple on top.

35.d: Trout ponds on the Uhl river, one of the old fishing centres of Himachal.
35.t: Angling needs a permit from the fisheries office.

35.d: Follow the river upstream from Barot through villages and forest.

49.d: A giant statue on the hill above the lake and caves where Padmasambhava is said to have meditated.

140.d: A hilltop temple of the Suket royal family with views over the Balh valley.

6.d: A temple on the ridge above Haripurdhar with views to Churdhar.

129.d: An old royal tank and garden in the middle of Nahan.
A flat walk around the top of the town with views over the plains — locals walk it every evening.
Ruins of a Gorkha-era fort on a hilltop above Nahan, reached by a steep path.

95.d: The small sacred tank next to Renuka lake, dedicated to Renuka's son Parshuram.
A small zoo by the lake, part of the Renuka sanctuary.

96.d: The riverbank right below the gurudwara — sit by the Yamuna in the evening.

99.d: Stone temples of the old town, drowned by the Bhakra reservoir, rise out of the water when the level drops in spring.
99.t: Only visible when the water is low.

99.d: A high bridge over the Satluj gorge on the Bilaspur–Ghumarwin road.

102.d: A temple built by Sansar Chand's queen with Kangra-style wall paintings inside.
The ruined palace-fort of the Katoch rulers on a hill above the Beas, built in 1758.
One of the biggest open grounds in Himachal, where the famous Holi fair is held.

131.d: The summer court of Raja Sansar Chand, about 2 km from town. The building is crumbling but still has some old paintings.
The Beas slows down at Nadaun — sit by the river, watch the anglers, or try a gentle stretch of rafting.
An old Shiva temple by the Beas, which locals link to the Pandavas.
India's first notified heritage village and its neighbour — old mansions and cobbled lanes.

85.d: Walk along the Parvati from Kasol and cross the footbridge into the pine forest — quieter the further you go from the market.

110.d: A small old monastery near Jispa, known for its masked chham dance in summer.
110.img: Top Gemur Gompa Lahaul Jun24 A7CR 00198.jpg

110.d: A small high-altitude lake beside the Manali–Leh road beyond Darcha, often still and mirror-like in the morning.
110.t: You are close to 4,000 m — go slowly.

50.d: Kibber is the base for winter snow leopard spotting in the high valleys around the village, run by local guides and homestays.
50.t: Very cold (−20 °C at night). Book only with local Kibber guides.
